reconciled_inputs.structure_note: Fuel-cycle developer in transition (playbook: contract-book build for fuel-cycle services + milestone rNPV for the new plant). The 3 years hold only the existing core: the LEU trading book (TENEX/Orano-sourced SWU resold under the firm book) and Technical Solutions, as a segment_build, less unallocated corporate cost (incl. stock comp, GAAP), ex expansion costs. FY2028 is the first year without Russian LEU for US customers, so it is a run-off level the engine can fade from (EBIT ~$7M); the trading book itself ends by 2030, and corporate overhead is absorbed by the plant thereafter, so carrying the small FY2028 NOPAT forward is a close approximation (DCF TV share 20%). The Piketon build-out is an rNPV adjustment in three programmes (initial LEU ~1.2M SWU; HALEU 12 MTU/yr with the DOE $900M task order as probability-weighted milestones discounted at a near-government rate; a phase-2 option) with post-horizon capex as dev costs; pre-horizon capital deployment, the September offering, Westerman's cash price, core cash and interest to the horizon and a 50% chance of a ~$400M raise are in net_debt_horizon. Westerman is an equity adjustment at its 2026-10-16 purchase price. Round 2 adds two equity adjustments: pension/OPEB obligations (-$56.6M after tax, 10-Q balance sheet) and a tax correction to the rNPV (+$81.5M: bonus-depreciation shield on build capex less 21% tax on the DOE milestones, which the rNPV left pre-tax); the custom legs carry the same two items, and the bull state of (b) no longer counts warrant-exercise cash. Legs: engine DCF 0.40 (core + rNPV + net cash), custom (b) market-share states 0.25 and (e) cash floor plus build option 0.25 (the forecasters' own weights for these methods), EV/EBITDA 0.10 cross-check (method-fit cap). The General Matter private mark is left out (weight 0; judgment call for Kilian). Contracts: empty - the DOE task order is milestone-contingent and its cash is not in the core years, so the engine's contracts block (which removes the cash flows from the years) would not value it; it sits in milestones_pv instead.

model.reasoning: Playbook primary methods: contract-book build for fuel-cycle services (the trading book as a segment_build from the firm LEU book, TENEX/Orano supply limits and segment margins) and a milestone rNPV for the new capacity (three programmes with build/demand phases, dated post-horizon capex as dev costs, DOE milestones as probability-weighted milestones_pv). The engine DCF (0.40, tested weight) values that core plus the rNPV and net cash; the method-fit rule (EBITDA margin 3.6%, net cash 29% of cap) is met with methods (a) milestone rNPV, (b) market-share states, (c) reverse DCF check and (e) cash floor plus option. Leg weights are the forecasters' own (0.25/0.25 custom, 0.10 cross-check; no weight moved: blend-weight README covers DCF vs P/E only). Cross-check: 6.0x NTM EBITDA vs the 14.0x peer median (BWXT/CEG/VST), a 57% discount for a finite-life stream; at the horizon the build-out is worth ~$0.1B risked in this set vs ~$1.3B implied by the price (reverse DCF). Labelled estimates (confidence; variant): SWU deck $200 rising 2%/yr (medium); LEU peak $275M (low; 1.0-1.5M SWU); HALEU $350/SWU on 0.49M SWU (low; $17M/MTU incl. feed would cut it sharply); 45% plant margin from Urenco 34.4% H1-26 / 38.4% FY25 EBITDA (verified) uplifted for new contracts near $200 (medium); capex ~$2.3B (low; Orano-like -> $59.92); probabilities 0.72/0.56/0.35 from the 1-in-4 US base rate lifted for DOE funding (medium); DOE milestones PV $640M at 5.5% (medium; 10% -> $590M); net cash at horizon $550M incl. 0.5 x $400M raise (medium); Westerman at its $116M purchase price (high). No conglomerate discount: Westerman is valued at an arm's-length price paid 4 days before the as-of date and is an operating supplier to the core build, not a holdco stake; variant with a 10% discount: -$0.5/share. Round 2 (engine $45.35 vs $46.07 in round 1): added pension/OPEB -$56.6M after tax (10-Q, high confidence), a tax correction +$81.5M (bonus-depreciation shield less tax on DOE milestones; low confidence; variants $44.09 / $42.46) and removed warrant-exercise cash from the (b) bull state (medium). Legs: DCF $34.31 (0.40, engine), EV/EBITDA 6.0x $36.90 (0.10), (b) $58.46 (0.25), (e) $53.31 (0.25); weights unchanged from round 1 and the forecasters' own (no tested evidence for the custom legs; the blend-weight results cover DCF vs P/E only). Year 3 (FY2028) is a run-off year, not a peak-capex or trough-margin year of an ongoing business (build capex sits in the rNPV); after year 3 the 6x multiple implies the core stream ends by ~2030. Scenarios: bear $26.53 (0.30) / base $45.35 (0.45) / bull $70.37 (0.25).
